Everything Blogkit shows comes from the front matter at the top of each post. Four fields matter most.

```yaml
---
title: "Required"
date: "2026-10-02"                # required, YYYY-MM-DD
categories: [Blogkit, Writing]    # broad: shown on cards, used for filtering
tags: [front-matter, tags]        # specific: drives the tag cloud and related posts
author: "Avery Kestrel"           # matches a name in authors.yml
---
```

A post without `title` or `date` is skipped (a warning is printed while rendering), and `draft: true` keeps a post out of the archive and tags.

### Categories Versus Tags

| | Categories | Tags |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Scope | Broad: language, subject, type | Specific: the concept in this post |
| Example | `Tutorial`, `R` | `front-matter`, `pagination` |
| Where you see them | Cards and the homepage category cloud | Sidebar tag cloud, tags page, post footer |
| How many | 1 to 3 | 3 to 6 |

Keep tags lowercase and hyphenated (`related-posts`, not `Related Posts`). Blogkit lowercases them anyway, but consistent names mean one tag instead of three near-duplicates.

### How Related Posts Are Chosen

Under every post you see up to five related ones. Blogkit scores each other post by the tags and categories it shares with the current one. A shared feature counts for more when **few** posts have it, so a rare tag such as `related-posts` says more than a common one such as `quarto`. Categories count half as much as tags. Posts with no overlap are never shown, so a post with unusual tags may have fewer than five.

In practice: reuse a tag when two posts really are about the same thing, and add one specific tag to every post. Related posts improve as your tagging does.

### Where Tags Appear

- The **sidebar** tag cloud, sized by how many posts use each tag.
- The **tags page**: click a tag to see its posts, ten per page by default (`per-page:` in `_quarto.yml`).
- A **Tags** row under each post body.
